links.outcome: Local diagnostic accuracy of FDA-cleared AI DR screening versus reference standard
links.effect: The system yielded favorable performance measures in the study population regarding detection accuracy; concluded LumineticsCore was a reliable screening test for DR in the study population.
links.quote: The system yielded favorable performance measures in the study population regarding detection accuracy.

links.outcome: AI DR screening performance in predominantly non-White population with comorbidity-stratified analyses
links.effect: Performance evaluated in a population that was 69.0% African American, 13.1% Hispanic, 10.7% White; system found reliable for DR detection in this population.
links.quote: The LumineticsCore system was found to be a reliable screening test for the detection of DR in the study population.

links.outcome: Follow-up attendance among patients with positive AI screen results
links.effect: 29.8% of patients with positive screen results did not attend their scheduled ophthalmology visit.
links.quote: It was found, however, that although most patients with a positive screen had ophthalmology referrals placed, 29.8% of patients with positive screen results did not attend their scheduled ophthalmology visit.

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the clinical implementation and diagnostic accuracy of an FDA-cleared AI screening system (LumineticsCore) deployed in a real-world clinic with a predominantly non-White population, tracking follow-up adherence, but it does not compare or test a specific deployment guardrail practice.
